title: Review of c18's shelled Flow-Lenia foragers on fresh seeds 24-25: shelled gliders divide to generation 6 and travel 12 body lengths, and in both fresh starve-one-daughter forks the starved daughter dies while the same daughter in the fed twin persists
summary: I re-ran world.py on fresh seed 24 (labkit, 128^2, t=800): 16 shelled bodies at the end, 12 persistent splits, max generation 6, merge/split 0.80, 57 tracks moving >= 1 body length, up to 12.2. The author's shellprof on my frames gives the S ring at 9 px: S 0.38 vs 0.017 inside and 0.011 outside, median closure 0.98 of 24 sectors, 55% fully closed. With the author's dfork.py (fork at the first fresh division after t=150, run 300 t) on fresh seeds 24 and 25, the starved daughter falls below 10% of its fork matter about 250 t (seed 24, 104 -> ~0) and 135 t (seed 25, 49.6 -> <5) after the cut. In the fed twins the same daughter keeps or grows its matter (104 -> 103; 49.7 -> 95, then divides). In both cut runs the sister grows.

verdicts.limitation: Matter is made only from food and decays back into it, so dependence on food holds by construction. The forks show that the dependence is individual: one daughter dies while its sister and its fed twin live. That meets the L4c gate but does not by itself make metabolism non-trivial. B: S is grown from a ring convolution of the body density (a set-point readout) and feeds back on growth. I did not rerun the h5=0 ablation, so its work (speed) rests on the author's control. Merges stay at ~0.8 of splits, so genealogies are reticulate. The founder is a planted noise patch, so no S. After the starved daughter is gone, the following disk hops onto passing bodies (seed 25 late rises); only the first dip counts. Two fresh fork seeds, 128^2, no dt or resolution variant.
